interpretation_limits: Installed feature/help/version and same libmpi.so.12 resolution do not prove actual MPICH interception or GPU collector support.

Unitrace LevelZero help promises demangled kernel names; runtime Kokkos label mapping is unproven. Compiler functor identities may map CalcRHS/SurfaceExchange source lambdas. All four bulk subsets share the same CalcRHS callsite and cannot be assigned solely by kernel name.

Native task queues contain no proven per-task or per-stage profiler regions. Initialization/final output kernels are captured; exact RK boundaries cannot be asserted from tool help. Conditional/session controls exist but no application ITT/Pcontrol collection markers were added.

Per-thread4096 event buffering does not cap total file volume. MPI_Testall polling can produce large traces and perturb progress even for selected ranks; all96-rank Chrome tracing is deliberately not proposed first.

No cross-node timestamp alignment is proven. Installed mergetrace.py concatenates events without clock synchronization and may modify malformed input JSON; preserve raw files, validate first, and never repair them in place.

MPI nonblocking post intervals overlapping GPU work do not alone demonstrate asynchronous communication progress. MPI_Testall observes completion later and cannot precisely timestamp when the transfer became ready.
The available MPI shim exports needed MPI calls and resolves the same MPICH family, but actual interception/ABI behavior and combined GPU+MPI collection remain untested.
Selected-rank traces can explain local exposed wait and kernel costs; a whole-job critical path requires additional validated coverage/clock alignment.

Changing the profiling-module environment can replace byte-different C++ runtime libraries; absolute invocation avoids that explicit module mutation but does not itself prove the launched process library map.

review.scope: Installed-tool facts and limited earlier-profile scope; no successful native GPU collection or global critical-path claim.
